hallucinations: Building pi in a World of Slop
There is zero observability, zero model choice, and almost zero extensibility in proprietary coding agent CLI tools.
Claude Code evolving from a simple TUI into a complex 3-iteration UI renderer with unpredictable context management.
Major maintainers like Lil' Bro (git-auth) and OpenClaw repositories had to close issue and PR trackers due to agentic spam.
Building 3D visualization tools to cluster and sift through thousands of garbage issues and PR texts.
Amazon service downtime and Windows quality issues attributed to rapid AI code integration.
Agent swarms generating 100k lines of code per day off the chart while human review capacity remains flat.
Mario built 'pi' with four core tools (read, write, edit, bash) and less than 1,000 tokens of system prompt and tool definitions.
Frontier models are RL-trained extensively and already know what a coding agent is; they don't need 10,000 tokens of instruction.
Community members built extensions like pi-messenger, pi-nes, and pi-doom inside pi sessions using hot reload.
None of this is about pi. I want you to retake control of your tools and workflows. Build your own.
Friction builds understanding and taste. This is where you actually learn.
We are in the fuck around and find out phase of (coding) agents
Amazon and other major corps have experienced massive production incidents due to unchecked AI coding bots.
Terminal-Bench scores higher on benchmarks than native model harnesses without file tools or subagents.
Graph comparisons showing agent code output skyrocketing past human review limits.
Frequent releases changing system prompts, tool definitions, and rendering logic in tools like Claude Code.
